section_summary: This section comprises the monthly political and economic reports from the American Embassy in Tokyo for February and March 1938 (Despatches No. 2816 and No. 2910, containing Reports No. 137 and No. 138), transmitted by Ambassador Joseph C. Grew to the Secretary of State. The February report provides comprehensive coverage of American and British representations concerning Japanese military depredations against foreign property in China, naval construction inquiries under the London Naval Treaty of 1936, the Alaskan salmon fisheries controversy, the disposal of Japanese contributions for USS Panay victims, military and aerial operations across China, Soviet-Japanese border incidents, Axis diplomatic coordination, and domestic legislative and economic developments in Japan, including the National General Mobilization Bill and crackdowns on liberalism. The opening portion of the March report details further US protests over air attacks on American mission and commercial properties in China, the evacuation and disruption of the Chinese Salt Administration, the formal presentation of the $2.2 million US indemnity claim for the USS Panay incident, and the settlement of the Alaskan fisheries dispute.

subfiles.about: Ambassador Grew transmits the Tokyo Embassy's monthly report No. 137 reviewing Japanese political, diplomatic, military, and economic developments during February 1938.
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Joseph C. Grew transmits Report No. 137 on conditions in Japan for February 1938 to Secretary of State Cordell Hull. The report reviews formal American representations regarding Japanese looting and occupation of mission properties, flag desecration, postal censorship, and smuggling in China, alongside joint British, American, and French inquiries into Japanese naval construction exceeding 1936 London Treaty limits. It documents negotiations over Bristol Bay salmon fishing, plans for a trust to hold Japanese contributions for USS Panay victims, military offensives across northern and central China, British representations over Shanghai customs and territorial waters, German recognition of Manchukuo, and Soviet frontier skirmishes. Domestically, it covers Diet debates, political tensions surrounding the National General Mobilization Bill and the state management of electric power, arrests of university liberals associated with the Popular Front, the ordinary budget passage, and foreign trade statistics, concluding with lists of Embassy despatches and telegrams sent during February.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 2816 Transmitting Report on Conditions in Japan During the Month of February, 1938 (Report No. 137)

subfiles.about: Ambassador Grew transmits the Tokyo Embassy's monthly report No. 138 reviewing Japanese foreign relations and internal affairs during March 1938.
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Joseph C. Grew transmits Report No. 138 covering conditions in Japan during March 1938 to the Secretary of State. This opening segment of the report concentrates on relations between the United States and Japan, recording representations regarding American extraterritorial rights in Manchuria, aerial attacks on American missions in Hankow, Chengchow, and Tenhsien, and bombing threats against Standard-Vacuum Oil installations in Wuchow. It also details diplomatic protests regarding Japanese military interference with the Chinese Salt Administration and the impairment of loan revenues securing American investments. The section concludes with the delivery on March 22 of the formal American demand for $2,214,007.36 in indemnification for the USS Panay sinking and the final negotiation and publication of the joint press communique regarding Alaskan salmon fisheries.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 2910 Transmitting Report on Conditions in Japan During the Month of March, 1938 (Report No. 138)
